note.question: Which outcomes-based reimbursement design best aligns a primary-care doctor and specialist when group contracts invite free riding and individual contracts may invite referral collusion?
note.overview: A healthcare payer designs contracts for a general practitioner and specialist whose quality choices are strategic complements or substitutes through patient health and referrals. Providers may play noncooperatively, free ride under a group contract, or collude and split gains through Nash bargaining.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The principal offers outcome-contingent individual or group contracts; providers accept if participation constraints hold; providers then choose care-quality decisions, either noncooperatively, with group-contract free riding, or under profitable collusion; health signals realize and payments are made. Primary-care quality changes both population health and downstream specialist volume. Separate contracts can turn extra referrals into a transferable gain from collusion.
